title: What’s this? — things around you
goal: Name the things around you, point to what’s near and what’s far, and meet the little -টা ending that turns “a book” into “the book”.
bekal: ask এটা কী? and answer it
tell apart এটা (this), ওটা (that, far), and সেটা (that, the one just mentioned)
deny identity with নয়, not with না
use adjectives, which never change form

dialogs.title: কথোপকথন — Mitali shows the room
dialogs.intro: Mitali takes Ani to her room on the second floor. Watch the -টা ending that appears again and again: it sticks to things when it’s clear which one is meant — exactly like English “the” in “the door”, except it goes at the end of the word.

lines.speaker: মিতালি:
lines.id: This is your room. The door is new.

lines.speaker: মিতালি:
lines.id: That’s a mirror. And this is a wardrobe.

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: The wardrobe is big. Where’s the window?

lines.speaker: মিতালি:
lines.id: It’s over there. The window is small, but the light is good.
lines.literal: that — the-one. window-the — small, but — light — good.

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: What’s that on the table? A book?

lines.speaker: মিতালি:
lines.id: No, that’s not a book. It’s a photo album.
lines.literal: no, that — book — not. that — picture-of — album.

lines.speaker: মিতালি:
lines.id: Here it is, the key is in the door. And this lamp is old.
lines.literal: this — the-one, key-the — door-in. and — this — lamp-the — old.

lines.speaker: আনি:
lines.id: That’s fine. The room is clean, that’s what matters.
lines.literal: fine — is. room-the — clean, that-very — big — matter.

lines.speaker: মিতালি:
lines.id: The towel is new. And the water is in that jug.
lines.literal: towel-the — new. and — water — that — jug-in — is.

notes: **-টা is English “the” — but stuck on the end.** বই *bôi* means “book” in general; **বইটা** *bôiTa* means “the book”, the one we both know about. English uses a separate word (*a book* / *the book*); Bengali glues it on as an ending. ⚠️ English speakers tend to forget it, because nothing at the end of an English noun does this job. -টা **never** means “whose” — ownership has its own ending, -র, which is Unit 4’s business.

**There are three endings, and choosing is easy.** **-টা** for anything, everyday, the most common — use it when in doubt. **-টি** means the same but sounds gentler and is written more than spoken; use it for something you respect or for small children (মেয়েটি — the girl). **-খানা** for flat, wide things: বইখানা, কাপড়খানা. For **people**, the ending is **-জন**: লোকজন, তিনজন ছাত্র.

⚠️ **Three pointing words, not two.** **এটা** *èTa* for something near the speaker (this). **ওটা** *oTa* for something far from both (that, over there). **সেটা** *séTa* for something **already mentioned** in the conversation — “that one”. English lumps the last two together as “that”, so সেটা needs practice of its own.

**এটা stands alone, এই attaches to a noun.** এটা বই = “this is a book”. **এই** বইটা = “**this** book”. Likewise ওটা versus **ওই**, and সেটা versus **সেই**. ⚠️ One of the most common beginner mistakes is saying *এটা বইটা* — both at once. The correct form is এই বইটা.

⚠️ **Denying identity uses নয়, not না.** Since “this is a book” has no verb, its negative isn’t a verb negative either. এটা বই। → এটা বই **নয়**। (this is not a book). **না** negates real verbs — আমি বুঝি না (I don’t understand) — which is Unit 6’s business. For now: **নয় = is not**, **না = do not**.

**Bengali adjectives never change form.** বড় ঘর (big room), বড় বই (big book), বড় মেয়ে (big girl) — one form for all. No gender, no plural, no endings to memorize. And they go **before** the noun, just as in English: লাল কলম = red pen.

**Many names for modern things come straight from English**, and you already know them: টেবিল, চেয়ার, ব্যাগ, ফোন, ল্যাপটপ, বাস, ট্রেন, স্কুল, ডাক্তার, হাসপাতাল. ⚠️ Say them with Bengali sounds, not English ones — ফোন is *phon* with a pure rounded o, not “fohn”. Slipping into an English accent actually makes you harder to understand.

grammars.title: Pointing words and their endings
after: **Plurals are formed with -গুলো** *-gulo* for things and **-রা** *-ra* for people: বইগুলো (the books), ছাত্ররা (the students). ⚠️ But the plural is **often not marked at all** when the number is already clear from another word — অনেক বই (many book), তিনটা বই (three book). English speakers want to add the plural every time; Bengali sees no need.

grammars.title: The most common adjectives
after: ⚠️ **গরম means hot, and also warm, and also spicy** — context decides. গরম চা is hot tea; আজ খুব গরম means “it’s very hot today”. For the spiciness that bites your tongue, people more often say **ঝাল** *jhal*, a word you’ll badly need in Unit 12.

blocks.title: ⚠️ পানি or জল? One word, two countries
items: Water is **পানি** *pani* in Bangladesh and **জল** *jôl* in West Bengal (Kolkata). Both are correct Bengali, both are understood everywhere, but the choice feels like an ID card: পানি sounds Bangladeshi, জল sounds Kolkata.
The same split shows up in a few other everyday words: invitation **দাওয়াত** *daoat* (Bangladesh) versus **নিমন্ত্রণ** *nimôntrôn* (Kolkata); aunt **খালা** *khala* versus **মাসি** *mashi*.
This course deliberately uses both, so your ear gets used to them. If you must pick one, pick the one used by the people you talk to most.

blocks.text: One pattern you can use right away to ask about anything: **এটা কী?** (what’s this?), **ওটা কার?** (whose is that?), **এটা কোথায়?** (where is this?), **এটার দাম কত?** (how much is this?). Every Bengali question word starts with the letter **ক**, and once you notice that, they’re much easier to learn — like English wh- words: কী, কে, কোথায়, কখন, কেন, কীভাবে, কত, কোন।

exercises.prompt: Add the -টা ending to the word in brackets.

items: Something far away across the street: ____ কী?
Something you were just talking about: ____ ভালো।
Something right under your nose: ____ আমার ব্যাগ।

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the right order.

answers: এটা বই নয়। — ঘরটা খুব সুন্দর। — চাবিটা কোথায়? — দরজাটা নতুন আর জানালাটা ছোট। — বইটা টেবিলে আছে।
এটা কী? — ওটা কলম নয়। — আলমারিটা বড়। — চাবিটা কোথায়? — এই ঘরটা পরিষ্কার। — ওই বইগুলো নতুন।
